target.title: fix(router): describe re-review comment upsert
target.body:
## Summary

- make the `@clawsweeper re-review` acknowledgement describe the durable review comment's real create-or-update behavior
- cover both the missing-comment creation path and the existing-comment update path with regression assertions

Fixes #581.

## What to review

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `src/repair/comment-router-core.ts` | Replace the assumption that a durable review comment already exists with mutually exclusive create-if-needed or update-in-place wording. |
| `test/repair/comment-router-core.test.ts` | Assert both alternatives and reject the former existing-comment and sequential-lifecycle assumptions. |

Diffstat: 2 files changed, 7 insertions, 3 deletions.

## How it works

The command acknowledgement now mirrors the publication contract: when the queued review finishes, ClawSweeper creates the durable review comment if none exists or updates the existing durable comment in place.

This does not change dispatch or publication behavior; it corrects the immediate status text shown after a valid re-review request.

## Real behavior proof

Using the same `re_review` command input against the renderer on `origin/main` and this branch:

Before (`origin/main` at `6248fba9f8cdbea81b9ffb8aefb15a95cf0d3d3a`):

```text
Result: the existing ClawSweeper review comment will be edited in place when the review finishes.
```

After (`d4ef85a3773808b9fda4a122d44fddb6582da802`):

```text
Result: when the review finishes, ClawSweeper will create the durable review comment if needed or update the existing comment in place.
```

The proof manifest binds both captures to the exact base and head SHAs.

## Testing

- `pnpm run build:all && pnpm run lint && pnpm run format:check && pnpm run check:active-surface && pnpm run check:limits`
- focused renderer regression under Node 24.18.0
- kanarienkrebs TS runtime validation: layer active, test exercised, no diagnostics
- marmorkrebs/Stryker on changed line 2166: 1 mutant killed, 0 survived (100%)
- complete unit, repair, changed-coverage, and full-coverage commands were executed locally before the final rebase; the changed renderer test and coverage thresholds pass. The macOS run also hit unrelated deadline/network-sensitive assertions, including failures reproduced on the then-current untouched `origin/main`; the GitHub Linux matrix remains the authoritative clean-CI check on the final head.

## Not included

- review queue scheduling or latency changes
- durable review comment publication logic
- changes to the existing in-place update behavior once a durable comment exists

## Risk and mitigation

Risk is limited to public acknowledgement copy. The regression test pins the mutually exclusive create-or-update wording, while the before/after renderer capture verifies the actual emitted text.

Closes #594

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where contributors supplying screenshot-only real-behavior proof would have that evidence treated as unviewable by ClawSweeper's network-disabled review sandbox.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper now hydrates linked PNG, JPEG, WebP, and GIF proof through the existing bounded media download path. Downloaded images are exposed directly for local inspection, while videos retain their existing ffprobe and contact-sheet processing. Local-range reviews continue skipping all host media downloads.

## User Impact

Screenshot-only evidence can now be assessed on its merits instead of being structurally classified as insufficient solely because the reviewer cannot access the network. Existing video proof behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Before the fix, the focused regression could not discover or hydrate a PNG proof URL, while the identical MOV URL was recognized.
- `pnpm run build && node --test test/review-prompt-policy.test.ts`: 31/31 passed. Coverage includes image discovery, image artifact preparation, no video-tool invocation for images, mixed image/video ordering, preserved video-only hook behavior, and existing ffprobe/contact-sheet processing.
- Real production-helper proof on macOS 26.0.1 with Node 24.16.0: served the repository's tracked PNG over a localhost HTTP server and ran the built media preparation helper with the real curl command. Result: `status=prepared`, `kind=image`, `downloaded=true`, `bytes=1478360`, `metadataCreated=false`, `contactSheetCreated=false`, `manifestArtifacts=1`; the server recorded an HTTP 200 GET.
- `pnpm run check`: passed, including build, lint, 1,180 unit tests with 0 failures, repair tests, changed and full coverage suites, and formatting.
- Limitation: no live GitHub-hosted ClawSweeper review decision was run; validation covers the production media hydration boundary, generated manifest, prompt guidance, and full local test suite.

target.title: test(repair): add hermetic automerge end-to-end flow
target.body:
## What this adds

A repository-owned, repeatable automerge end-to-end harness that runs the production planner, executor, publisher, applicator, exact-head verdict, and comment-router merge before changes reach `main`.

GitHub and Codex are stateful simulators. The production CLIs, Git clone/fetch/checkout/commit/push, Corepack/pnpm install, artifact-only job handoff, token separation, validation, exact-head binding, squash merge, and idempotent replay run for real against a tiny target repository.

## Local and CI entrypoints

```bash
pnpm e2e:automerge:container
pnpm e2e:automerge:container -- --scenario planning-head-drift
pnpm e2e:automerge -- --list-scenarios
```

The container uses Node 24.13.0 and a versioned Docker Hub base pinned by digest. It is capped at 8 GiB with no additional swap and 1024 PIDs. Git, Python, CA certificates, and Corepack live in the reusable base, while project dependencies remain a lockfile-keyed layer.

Published base:

`masonxhuang/clawsweeper-automerge-e2e-base:node24.13.0-bookworm-20260718@sha256:26a4e98237cc595b10166b27fc3e6342e805fed0446602e1960357ef6f82bba2`

The outer container keeps its default root user so the production validator can create its nested user/mount namespace. Target commands still start only after the validator drops every capability. The wrapper does not use privileged mode or add capabilities, and it restores artifacts to the invoking host UID afterward.

`.github/workflows/automerge-e2e.yml` runs all six scenarios on the production-class Blacksmith execution runner for relevant repair, harness, package-manager, and workflow changes. Untrusted fork pull requests do not receive that runner.

## Historical before/after proof

The `ci-regression-29623139111` scenario reconstructs [Actions job 88022196284](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29623139111/job/88022196284) with a tiny real Git repository, Node 24.13.0, and pnpm 11.2.2. The root cause does not depend on the OpenClaw source graph.

To isolate the linked index-identity defect from the earlier Yarn-shim defect in the historical revision, a test-only Corepack proxy adds the missing `pnpm` selector. An index-stat mutator changes only Git's administrative stat cache; content and tree remain unchanged.

- Before, candidate `7be2e4915b4b1d9aa953ccfe359cea670a4616ec`: reproduces `target dependency setup mutated checkout identity`.
- After, current stack with the same mutation: completes edit, validation, push, exact-head verdict, squash merge, and replay.

## Scenarios

- happy path
- tracked dependency-setup mutation rejection
- pending checks becoming green
- planning-to-execution head drift
- stale exact-head verdict
- 2026-07-18 runtime-identity regression

## Validation

- [Blacksmith production automerge flow](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29635545577): all six scenarios passed and proof artifacts uploaded.
- Final local root-container run: 6/6 scenarios passed.
- Container/workflow contract tests: 5/5 passed.
- Repair tests: 924 passed, 3 environment skips.
- Changed coverage: 100% lines, 88.61% branches, 100% functions for the changed target.
- Full coverage: 77.74% lines, 73.41% branches, 86.00% functions.
- Build, all lint gates, format check, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Full unit status: 1331 passed and 1 environment skip; the same unrelated 3-second `apply-runtime-budget` timing assertion failed in the initial local full run and both GitHub full-suite attempts, while the isolated file passed 8/8 on both local reruns.

## Crabbox status

Direct AWS Crabbox has been attempted twice. Provider `aws`, lease `cbx_76e570182550` remained in SSH bootstrap for six minutes; provider `aws`, lease `cbx_cab52b2e734f` remained there for 2 minutes 21 seconds. Neither attempt started the repository command. Both leases were interrupted and confirmed cleaned up/released. Crabbox is therefore supported by the checked-in container entrypoint but is not claimed as a completed proof for this PR.

Stack 3/3. Base: `feature/automerge-production-fixes`.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where repair workers could stop with `target dependency setup mutated checkout identity` after a normal dependency install. This occurred when pnpm populated ignored runtime files through tracked workspace links or normalized the non-Git permission bits of a tracked executable.

## Why This Change Was Made

Checkout identity now uses Git's executable/non-executable mode semantics for tracked regular files and records authenticated references for tracked symlinks to tracked files or matching tracked workspaces. Untracked, mismatched, external, and non-`node_modules` workspace links remain fail-closed.

## User Impact

Repair workers can continue past dependency setup when the install only creates expected ignored runtime state or normalizes Git-equivalent executable permissions. Actual tracked source changes, executable-bit changes, later ignored runtime changes, and unsafe symlink targets are still detected.

## Evidence

- Both regression tests failed on `main` with `target dependency setup mutated checkout identity` before the fix and pass after it.
- Focused coverage includes tracked cross-workspace links, Git-equivalent `0775` to `0755` normalization, tracked source mutation, executable-bit removal, later ignored runtime mutation, and the existing untracked/mismatched/external symlink rejection cases.

target.title: Screenshot proof is never hydrated, so realBehaviorProof is always "insufficient" for image-only evidence
target.body:
<!-- issue-loop-fingerprint: a36d80b49a57013d0cd469a0800649483eda18bbe1a4df61b382090bf547ede1 -->

I ran into this while using `Bash`: The review prompt says screenshots are valid real-behavior proof and that the reviewer may open linked artifacts from the provided scratch directory. But prepareMediaProofArtifacts() hydrates video URLs only, so linked images are never downloaded into proofScratchDir, and the reviewer runs sandbox read-only where sandboxPolicy() hardcodes networkAccess:false - so it cannot fetch them itself either. The reviewer therefore cannot view screenshot proof and, following the prompt's own rule ("insufficient when the evidence is ... unviewable"), rates realBehaviorProof insufficient with needsContributorAction=true. Video-proven PRs are unaffected. This is not local-only: .github/workflows/sweep.yml runs the review job with --codex-sandbox read-only.

I expected Linked screenshots should be hydrated into proofScratchDir (already passed to codex via --add-dir) so the read-only reviewer can open them locally, exactly as linked videos are today - and screenshot-proven PRs should be assessable on their merits.
Instead, Image URLs are filtered out before hydration, so nothing is downloaded. The sandboxed reviewer has neither a local copy nor network access, cannot view the evidence, and rates realBehaviorProof=insufficient / needsContributorAction=true no matter how good the screenshots are.

I traced this to proofVideoUrlsFromContext() keeps only URLs ending in VIDEO_PROOF_EXTENSIONS, so prepareMediaProofArtifacts() returns early for image-only proof and writes nothing to proofScratchDir. Since the reviewer runs sandbox read-only and sandboxPolicy() hardcodes networkAccess:false for that mode, the model has neither a local copy nor network, making screenshot proof structurally unviewable.
I verified that with Red-green on a clean clone of upstream main at c17589a56c, using the project's own exported test hook and test helpers: a .png proof URL returns [] from proofVideoUrlsFromContextForTest (RED - never hydrated) while an otherwise identical .mov URL returns the URL (GREEN control - hydrated). Only the extension differs. Result: 2 pass / 0 fail.

Reproduction: Clean clone of openclaw/clawsweeper at c17589a56c, then pnpm install && pnpm run build. Add test/zz-repro.test.ts mirroring the existing video assertion in test/review-prompt-policy.test.ts:274, changing only the file extension, and run: node --test test/zz-repro.test.ts

});
test("identical video proof IS hydrated", () => {
  const mov = "https://github.com/user/repo/releases/download/proof/demo.mov";
  assert.deepEqual(proofVideoUrlsFromContextForTest(ctx(mov))<truncated>
Environment: openclaw/clawsweeper main at c17589a56c, clean clone, pnpm install && pnpm run build, node --test, macOS. target.body:
<!-- issue-loop-fingerprint: 4105449e12232426bef5b4e88d40475dc4c13e8ed52d7f1c9d80e3ab9513e086 -->

I ran into this while using `GitHub`: On PR #576, `@clawsweeper re-review` was accepted into the exact-review queue before any durable ClawSweeper review comment existed, but the command-status reply promised that the existing review comment would be edited in place. Both enqueue-only workflows completed successfully; this report is about the inaccurate acknowledgement, not review-queue latency.

I expected the acknowledgement to remain accurate for both supported paths: create the first durable review placeholder when none exists, or update the existing durable review comment.
Instead, the successful re-review response always says that the existing ClawSweeper review comment will be edited in place, including when no durable review marker exists yet.

I traced this to the dispatched `re_review` branch of `renderResponse` emitting a fixed existing-comment sentence. Its inputs do not carry review-comment existence, while the documented review lifecycle supports both creating a marker-backed placeholder and editing an existing durable comment; the focused test currently asserts the fixed sentence.
I verified that with the live PR having two accepted `@clawsweeper re-review` commands, one surviving command-status acknowledgement, no durable `clawsweeper-review` marker, and no posted review. Both repository-dispatch workflow runs completed successfully in enqueue-only mode. Current `origin/main` unconditionally emits and tests the existing-comment sentence, while `docs/pr-review-comments.md` says a review shard creates a marker-backed placeholder when no durable comment exists.

The raw artifacts I used are: https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/576#issuecomment-4973212500 ; https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29362584394 ; https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29367358183 ; https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/blob/eda9768bd1b77cd6b0e3cb19199e1c2da8d78a7d/src/repair/comment-router-core.ts#L2155-L2169 ; https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/blob/eda9768bd1b77cd6b0e3cb19199e1c2da8d78a7d/test/repair/comment-router-core.test.ts#L3150-L3172 ; https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/blob/eda9768bd1b77cd6b0e3cb19199e1c2da8d78a7d/docs/pr-review-comments.md#L21-L33

target.title: fix(text): harden string helpers against small/degenerate inputs
target.body:
## Summary

Four internal string helpers violate their invariants on inputs outside their current call sites. Every present caller passes safe values, so these are latent hardening fixes rather than live production bugs. The patch also keeps mutation authorization fail-closed for malformed repeated `[bot]` identities.

## What to review

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/clawsweeper-text.ts` | `trimMiddle`: fall back to head truncation when the middle split has no room |
| `src/repair/text-utils.ts` | `compactText`: omit the ellipsis when it cannot fit; `slug`: re-trim trailing dashes after slicing |
| `src/repair/comment-router-utils.ts` | `normalizeGitHubActor`: strip all trailing `[bot]` suffixes for idempotent requester grouping; document that mutation authorization still compares the submitted actor exactly |
| Matching test files | Pin the helper boundaries and prove repeated `[bot]` actors remain unauthorized |

## How it works

- `trimMiddle` delegates zero/negative head-tail budgets to the existing head-truncation helper.
- `compactText` returns only text when a three-character ellipsis cannot fit.
- `slug` removes trailing dashes again after applying its maximum-length slice.
- `normalizeGitHubActor` collapses repeated trailing bot suffixes for requester grouping only. `isAllowedMutationActor` deliberately does not call it and continues to compare the raw, case-normalized actor exactly.

## Real-behavior proof

Exact same helper calls on current `origin/main` (`923797712890`) and this branch (`f37871086e40`):

```text
                                         BEFORE                    AFTER
compactText("hello world", 2)            "..." (length 3)          "he" (length 2)
slug("a a", "x", 2), then slug again    "a-" -> "a"              "a" -> "a"
normalizeGitHubActor("x[bot][bot]")      "x[bot]" -> "x"          "x" -> "x"
trimMiddle(25 x characters, 20)          reports 125 removed       reports 5 removed
isAllowedMutationActor(repeated suffix)  false                     false
```

The paired local proof manifest records the full exact-revision JSON observations and hashes both artifacts.

## Testing

- Node 24.18.0: build, active-surface/limit checks, all oxlint lanes, and oxfmt check pass.
- Affected suites: 53 passed, 0 failed.
- `kanarienkrebs`: strict TypeScript runtime layer active; affected tests exercised; no diagnostics; PASS.
- `marmorkrebs --scope-lines --threshold 1`: 29/29 changed-line Stryker mutants killed; 0 survivors; 100%.
- The full local unit run passed 1,175 tests with 2 platform skips. The repair run passed 883 with 7 platform skips and hit two millisecond-deadline assertion failures that reproduce identically on untouched `origin/main` under the repository's pinned Node 24.18.0. Hosted CI remains the full-suite authority.

## Risk and scope

The helper fixes remain outside all current caller inputs. The main risk is broadening actor identity; the authorization-level regression explicitly proves that `clawsweeper[bot][bot]` remains rejected while a real trusted bot login remains accepted.

Closes #571.
Closes #572.
Closes #573.
Closes #574.

target.body:
`normalizeGitHubActor(login)` in `src/repair/comment-router-utils.ts:185` strips a single trailing `[bot]` via `/\[bot\]$/i`, so a doubled suffix leaves a residual that a second pass strips again.

Repro:
```
normalizeGitHubActor("x[bot][bot]") === "x[bot]"
normalizeGitHubActor("x[bot]")      === "x"        // => not idempotent
```
A normalizer should be idempotent. Loop/global-strip the suffix (though a doubled [bot] is rare in practice). Related: `stripEnvPrefix` in `repair/validation-command-utils.ts` has the same single-pass shape.

target.title: compactText: overflows maxLength for small caps (returns bare '...')
target.body:
`compactText(value, maxLength)` in `src/repair/text-utils.ts:1`: for `maxLength` in 0..2 the small-cap branch returns `slice(0, max(0, maxLength-3)) + '...'` = just `'...'` (length 3), which exceeds the requested cap.

Repro:
```
compactText("hello world", 2) === "..."   // length 3 > maxLength 2
```
Invariant: `compactText(s, n).length <= n`. Clamp the ellipsis to fit, or floor the cap.

target.title: slug: not idempotent — slice after trailing-dash trim can re-introduce a trailing dash
target.body:
`slug(value, fallback, maxLength)` in `src/repair/text-utils.ts:19` trims edge dashes and THEN `.slice(0, maxLength)`, so slicing on a `-` boundary re-introduces a trailing dash.

Repro:
```
slug("a a", "x", 2) === "a-"   // trailing dash
slug("a-", "x", 2)  === "a"    // => not idempotent: slug(slug(x)) !== slug(x)
```
Fix: trim trailing dashes AFTER the length slice (or re-trim post-slice).

target.title: trimMiddle: negative edge for maxLength<120 overflows output and reports impossible truncated count
target.body:
`trimMiddle(text, maxLength)` in `src/clawsweeper-text.ts:11` computes `edge = Math.floor((maxLength - 120) / 2)`, which goes **negative** for any `maxLength < 120`. The head/tail slices then take from the wrong ends and the reported "truncated N chars" count exceeds the input length.

Repro (property-test found via einsiedlerkrebs):
```
trimMiddle("x".repeat(25), 20)  =>  length 31 (> maxLength 20), text says "truncated 125 chars" for a 25-char input
```
Invariants violated: result length should be ~<= maxLength, and the reported removed-count should be in [0, text.length]. Guard `edge` to a sane minimum (and/or short-circuit when `maxLength` is below the header overhead).

target.title: fix(repair): bind automerge execution to planned head
target.body:
## Root cause

Automerge planning produced a deterministic result without recording the exact pull-request head it reviewed. Execution then read the live head and could continue against a newer contributor revision, crossing the planning/execution trust boundary.

## Changes

- Persist `reviewed_sha` in deterministic automerge results.
- Compare it with the live PR head before target clone, Codex, or push.
- Write a durable blocked report with `expected_head_sha`, `current_head_sha`, and `requeue_required: true` when the head moved.

## Validation

- `pnpm run build:all`
- all source/repair/script/dashboard lint gates
- repair tests and coverage gates passed
- container E2E `planning-head-drift` advances the contributor head after planning and proves execution stops before target checkout, Codex, or push

Stack 2/3. Base: `feature/automerge-target-runtime`.
